text:
This one was never as close as 1-0 through the middle of the second period suggested, and it never got closer. Boston controlled nearly everything at TD Garden, holding a 64-37 edge in shot attempts and 3.13 to 1.34 in expected goals. The Bruins deserved to win 81 percent of the time in simulated replays of every shot, and the 5-1 final over Philadelphia fit the way the game was played.

The goals came from pressure rather than luck. Pavel Zacha opened the scoring at 12:21 of the first on a wrist shot from David Pastrnak's pass, and Mason Lohrei made it 2-0 late in the second. Marat Khusnutdinov scored less than two minutes into the third, and after Porter Martone cut it to 3-1 on a power play, Casey Mittelstadt and Fraser Minten answered before the game could tighten. Minten finished with a goal and two assists, and JJ Peterka added two assists on a line that out-chanced Philadelphia badly.

Dan Vladar faced 32 shots and allowed five against an expected 3.13, which cost the Flyers nearly two goals compared with an average night. Jeremy Swayman had far less to do, stopping 14 of 15 shots, though that was close to what the chances warranted. Philadelphia's lone bright spot was Martone's power-play goal, one of only three real looks the Flyers generated all night.
